guide.summary: Register a Google Cloud OAuth client for Gmail API access, configure the consent screen with required branding and scopes, add authorized redirect URIs, enable Gmail API, and submit for verification. Note: gmail.readonly and most Gmail data scopes are RESTRICTED and additionally require an annual CASA security assessment; gmail.send is SENSITIVE (verification but no security assessment). Testing mode allows up to 100 test users, and test-user authorizations (and refresh tokens) expire after 7 days.

difficulty.verdict: Google verification is required for Gmail's sensitive and restricted scopes; restricted Gmail scopes (including gmail.readonly) additionally require an annual CASA security assessment by a Google-authorized third-party assessor (developer pays the assessor); manual review with undocumented timeline; strict redirect URI validation; incremental scope authorization recommended.

steps.title: Add Gmail scopes to OAuth consent screen
steps.action: In Data Access section, add required Gmail scopes (e.g., gmail.readonly, gmail.send) with justification
steps.human_because: Scope justification text requires human context about app functionality
steps.nuances: Best practice: request scopes incrementally at time of use. Classification matters: gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, gmail.insert, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing and https://mail.google.com/ are RESTRICTED; gmail.send is SENSITIVE; gmail.labels and the add-on action scopes are non-sensitive. Restricted scopes require verification plus a security assessment.

steps.title: Enable Gmail API
steps.action: Search for Gmail API in API Library and click Enable
steps.nuances: Required before making API calls. As of May 1, 2026 Gmail API quotas were updated for new projects: 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project, 6,000 quota units per minute per user, and an 80,000,000 units/day per-project billing threshold. Projects created before May 1, 2026 keep prior quotas.

steps.title: Submit for verification (and security assessment) before production launch
steps.action: Click Submit for Verification; provide justification demo video and per-scope justification for sensitive and restricted Gmail scopes; for restricted scopes complete a CASA security assessment through a Google-authorized assessor
steps.duration: 30-60 minutes preparation + review and assessment wait
steps.human_because: Requires recording demo video, writing scope justifications, and engaging a paid CASA-authorized assessor for restricted scopes
steps.nuances: Verification is required for sensitive and restricted scopes (gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.readonly and most other Gmail scopes are restricted). Restricted scopes additionally require a security assessment by a CASA-authorized independent assessor, which must be repeated annually; Google charges no fee for the assessment itself but the developer pays the authorized assessor (or uses the free Tier 1 self-scan where eligible). The 100 new-user cap applies to unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes for the entire lifetime of the project and cannot be reset. Re-verification is needed for new scopes or branding changes.

gotchas.title: Scope justification required for verification
gotchas.why_it_matters: Each sensitive/restricted Gmail scope needs individual justification with demo video; verification is rejected without a clear user-benefit explanation
gotchas.how_to_handle: Prepare per-scope justification documents and demo video showing user-facing functionality before submission

gotchas.title: Restricted Gmail scopes require an annual CASA security assessment
gotchas.why_it_matters: gmail.readonly and most other Gmail data scopes are RESTRICTED: verification alone is not enough — apps storing or transmitting restricted-scope data on servers must pass a security assessment by a CASA-authorized assessor, repeated annually. Google does not charge a fee, but the assessor does (Tier 2), and assessments can take weeks and cost money
gotchas.how_to_handle: Budget for the assessment early; minimize restricted scopes (gmail.send is only sensitive); check whether your use qualifies for Tier 1 self-scan; note the assessment must be redone each year

gotchas.title: Unverified apps are capped at 100 NEW users for the project's lifetime
gotchas.why_it_matters: Unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes get an unverified-app warning screen and a 100 new-user cap that applies over the entire lifetime of the project and cannot be reset or changed — even in production. Once exhausted, Google sign-in is disabled for your users
gotchas.how_to_handle: Add developers/testers as test users while in Testing (max 100 test users; test-user authorizations expire 7 days after consent); complete verification before exposing the app to real users

gotchas.title: Quota limits and exponential backoff
gotchas.why_it_matters: Gmail API quotas changed as of May 1, 2026 for new projects: 1,200,000 quota units/min/project, 6,000 quota units/min/user, 80,000,000 units/day/project billing threshold; per-method costs range from 1 unit (getProfile) to 100 units (messages.send); exceeding limits returns errors
gotchas.how_to_handle: Check the current quota page for your project's limits; monitor usage in Cloud Console; implement exponential backoff with jitter for all API calls

sources.title: Gmail API Scopes
sources.what_it_supports: Classification of all Gmail scopes: gmail.readonly/gmail.compose/gmail.modify/gmail.metadata/gmail.insert/gmail.settings.* and mail.google.com are restricted; gmail.send is sensitive; security assessment required when restricted-scope data is stored/transmitted on servers

sources.title: Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications
